evidence_quotes.name_asked_and_used: Rep: 'My name is Zang, I'm from Einstein moving.' Customer: 'Zane. Okay.' Name never used again in call.
evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this would take within the next 15 Five to ten minutes of your time' and asks 'Would that be okay?' but never frames the dependable quote promise or explicitly waits for confirmation before pivoting to concerns.
evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Rep asks 'Do you have any concerns or any important things that you wanted to answer during this call today?' — open-ended, not the two-concerns frame about on-time arrival or damage.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raises concern about moving only two bedrooms plus living/dining/kitchen items, not the full house. Rep acknowledges repeatedly but never digs deeper with 'tell me more about that' or silence. Moves to logistics checklist instead.
evidence_quotes.promises_delivered: Rep mentions 'no why damage coverage included' (No Worries Damage Coverage, 2000 dollars per move) and 'on time guarantee' with discount structure, but delivery is buried in a long pricing monologue, no permission lead-in asked, and On-Time terms are stated but the No Worries terms are vague ('repair, replace and reimburse'). No explicit discussion of what is included vs. add-on structure.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep never asks 'Does that put those to rest?' or equivalent.
evidence_quotes.concern_led_opening_and_logistics: Rep does not open with 'What items are you most concerned about?' Instead jumps to logistics checklist: address, bedrooms, square footage, parking, access concerns, box count. Some details gathered but concern-led frame is absent.
evidence_quotes.packing_and_box_count: Rep asks 'typical bax count based on your home size is 115 to 135 boxes. Do you feel that you fall within that range?' but does NOT ask 'Would you like us to pack your items into boxes for you?' Only box count is addressed.
evidence_quotes.value_days: No mention of day selection, pricing contrast, or date flexibility.
evidence_quotes.prep_and_temperature_check: No prep framing or 'How do you feel about that?' temperature check present.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: No rate lock mentioned. No explicit ask for the business. Call ends with customer saying she will send photos/videos another time and rep agrees to send estimate via email.
evidence_quotes.virtual_walkthrough_offer: Rep correctly identifies this as a 2333 sq ft house (over 1800 threshold) and offers virtual walkthrough: 'Normally, based on your home size we do a a virtual offer in that way' and 'Do you have time to complete the virtual walk for today.' Customer declines due to appointment and offers to send photos instead. Rep eventually says 'if ever you do have unavailable time feel free to let us know if you want us to send you a link or we can schedule for a virtual walkthrough. Anyway we're open Monday to Sunday at anytime.' This is a clean routing to walkthrough, though complicated by customer resistance.

top_strength: Rep correctly identified the move size (2333 sq ft) as requiring a virtual walkthrough and persistently offered the walkthrough option as the proper path forward rather than forcing a quote on incomplete information.
coaching_note: This call should have routed to walkthrough clean in the first three minutes — instead, rep spent 13+ minutes defending square-footage-based pricing and negotiating with the customer about estimation methods; the two-concerns question was never asked, neither promise was clearly framed with permission, and packing was never addressed. Master the walkthrough redirect as a clean, confident close rather than a fallback after customer pushback.
